figures.caption: Figure 4.5.1: Stereo audio codec AFE architecture.

references.sentence: As depicted in Fig. 4.5.1, the CODEC contains microphone PGAs, audio ΔΣ ADCs and DACs, speaker drivers and microphone bias generators.
Each audio input path contains front-end filters, a microphone PGA and a 3rdorder continuous-time ΔΣ ADC, as shown in Fig. 4.5.2(a).
A hybrid PGA, as shown in Fig. 4.5.2(a), is designed to overcome this hurdle.
The linearity and gain accuracy can be further improved with active feedback as illustrated in Fig. 4.5.2(b).
To reduce the noise, an alternative transconductance cell is detailed in Fig. 4.5.2(c), where transistor M2, current source I1 and inverting amplifier form the active feedback.
Compared to the transconductance cell with the conventional active feedback shown in Fig. 4.5.2(b), the number of components contributing noise in Fig. 4.5.2(c) is reduced by a half.
This ADC, as shown in Fig.4.5.3, uses a capacitor-feed-forward architecture with a direct-feedback path.
Each audio output path consists of a switched capacitor DAC, a low-pass filter, a PGA and Class-AB speaker drivers, as shown in Fig. 4.5.4.
The Class-AB amplifiers are implemented with an accurate quiescent current control scheme, as shown in Fig. 4.5.4.
The Class-AB amplifier in Fig. 4.5.4 further improves the quiescent current control by employing a replica of the driver and the output stage.
Figure 4.5.5 shows the spectra of the complete audio input path in line-in mode and the complete audio output path driving a 28Ω load.
The key measured results are summarized in Fig. 4.5.6.
Fabricated in a 0.13µm CMOS, the prototype stereo codec occupies an active area of 2.4mm2 (Fig. 4.5.7).
